blurbs.180-degrees: The only two Michelin star restaurant in the Baltics. A really nice experimental place on the Noblessner waterfront, where the tasting menu is built to surprise you course after course.
blurbs.annon: I love when they opened the restaurant, their motto was “food should be useful to the body”. Soviet Korean comfort food in Lasnamäe, fifteen minutes from the centre by bus. Spicy all the way through. You can't avoid the chili in any bite. The lamb soup could use more lamb, but it still hits the spot. It is open until 18:00, so you need to hurry.
blurbs.ariran: We pass by daily and somehow kept skipping it. A Korean restaurant on Telliskivi street run by the same owner for 34 years. He's from Korea, has lived most of his life in Estonia, and is sharp and multilingual. When you enter, show some respect. That isn't an easy business.
blurbs.badam: The most authentic Azerbaijani cooking in Tallinn. Kifta, dolma, traditional xangal, piti, plov, lamb plov. It is next to bus station. So on the way somewhere, or on the way back, it is great spot to stop by.
blurbs.baklazaan: Out on the way to the Nõmme bike route, which is a fine ride in itself. Good spot, delicious shashlik, solid Caucasian cooking.
blurbs.balta-chill: A hidden yard off Vana-Kalamaja that somebody has to tell you about. Graffiti on every board, and a room to match. It is a place made for chilling, which is the half of the name that says so. If the door does not open, knock. They might let you in.
blurbs.bekker-pagariari: The OG bakery, supplying bread and kringels to lots of places in town. The salted caramel one is ridiculous. The room itself has hidden corners, and it only gets cosier as the weather turns. Give a try to savoury and sweet pastries. If you are group of people, then order one of each. And share everything.
blurbs.borsch-ja-varenyk: A cozy place next to Taksopark for warm borscht, vareniki and other homemade Ukrainian dishes. Friendly staff and a welcoming vibe that makes it feel like grandma's kitchen.
blurbs.bruto-bakehouse: A bakehouse in the Old Town that lives for cookies. Thick, soft in the middle, and worth the walk. The pistachio one is the favourite.
blurbs.bueno-gourmet-kadriorg: Street food that feels honest and real. Everything is under €7, which is rare these days. Chilean-run, fair prices, strong taste. Kadriorg is a chill area to grab your food and eat outside, just don't forget a napkin.
blurbs.burger-box: Once just a small burger window next to the old Põhjala Speakeasy, it has kept its street-food soul while the menu got bolder. Prices stay wallet-friendly and the vibe is relaxed: vegan-friendly, dog-friendly, people-friendly.
blurbs.buxhowden-pagar: A really cool bakery out on the way to Viimsi. The savouries are filling and delicious.
blurbs.cafe-cape-town: Paul's place inside the market hall. Chillest dude, coolest vibes, and a must-see spot in town. Handmade South African pies. Now he is opening new place in Kadriorg, proper South African place. We are waiting.
blurbs.cafe-tempo: The place is in a cool spot, and it gets lots of sun. Most of menu is delicious, except the meat (last time 2026 may, still it needed work). But the vibes are great, service is excellent. Negroni is delicious.
blurbs.chakra: Most of you have tried this Indian kitchen from Bolt Food, but the Old Town room is special: a very old building, and a chef who moved to Estonia in 1992 and finally opened his own place in 2009. As chef Ventak said main ingredients in indian cuisine are onion, ginger, tomato and garlic. I recommend onion baji and whatever the waitresses recommends. They are good at their job and hospitality.
blurbs.chamber-tea: Masters of tea who know exactly what they are doing. A quiet room for anyone who takes the leaf seriously.
blurbs.chocolala: Award-winning chocolates made right here, with a small chocolate museum on Suur-Karja. There is a second spot in Telliskivi. A really cool place either way. Their hot chocolate is quite nice too if you are looking for something warm.
blurbs.crustum-bakery: The first bakery from the team behind La Boulangerie, and it has been feeding Mustamäe for years. A small, tucked-away neighbourhood place, so bring the map.
blurbs.dvin: Georgian food, honest and delicious, out in Kopli. Their khinkalis and napoleon cakes are my favourite. Prices are so cheap, you wouldn’t believe that it is possible in Tallinn. Thanks for existing.
blurbs.elman-bites: A kiosk in Telliskivi with really nice falafel. They also run experiments with beef liver and other cuts you don't usually see on a grill menu, so ask what's new. The owner is friendly and you would feel welcome.
blurbs.f-hoone: Breakfast, lunch, pizza and sandwiches, all day in one of the oldest buildings in Telliskivi. Everything is good in this place, pelmeni is the one everyone should order once. The name is the building: block F. The room is as good as the food and the terrace is as good as the room. Highly recommended.
blurbs.faehlmanni-kohvik: A corner cafe that has been on Faehlmanni a long time, and it is one of the nicest corners in the neighbourhood. Bakery, coffee and a really good brunch. Calm enough that you can sit and work there.
blurbs.faeton: As azeri I approve this place. Apart from shashliks, they serve proper Azerbaijani cuisine too. The qutab has a twist: filled with greens and mozzarella instead of the traditional herbs. Portions are huge, if you're dining solo, half a küftä might be plenty. After eating here, don’t forget to have a walk in Kadriorg park. Because you need to digest all the calories you would get.
blurbs.ferment: Two years ago this spot was the best spot. Unluckily Michael king of service left Estonia. But their pizza and bread are still super delicious. Ordering bread and dipping into everything you see is highly recommended. Probably they will open their doors again in summer. Michael, we miss you!
blurbs.fotografiska: Fine dining where everything comes from local producers, with their own beehives and their own fermentation. The green Michelin star is no joke, and the view from the top is worth the trip on its own. Also head chef also got young chef Michelin award.
blurbs.fotografiska-cafe: The ground floor of the Fotografiska building: a shop at the door, the museum one way, the restaurant upstairs, and this bakery filling the middle. Everything is baked on the spot, so it is worth stopping for the baker even if the museum is what brought you in. The room is a genuinely lovely place to sit with a laptop for a couple of hours.
blurbs.francois-boulangerie: François and his croissants are back on Härjapea street. Saturdays only. You order in advance and go and queue in front of the house. But don’t forget slavic squat. In order to take your order you have to trust your squatting skills.
blurbs.gobi: Modern Georgian cuisine in Rotermanni. Adjaruli and khinkali are the reasons to revisit the place again.
blurbs.gotsu-kyuho: A Korean restaurant that's been here a long time, known for its flavours, peppery spices and warm atmosphere. A little hidden gem for anyone craving authentic Korean food in the city.
blurbs.hans: Hans means my humble home. Not sure about this one. Sometimes it is super good, sometimes it disappointed. I heard from other people too, it is super delicious, but some said that they were disappointed too. Still give a try, I liked their beef.
blurbs.hell-hunt: Very good beers from Humalakoda, and the kitchen holds up too. The chicken strips and the fish and chips are both worth ordering.
blurbs.izakaya-taro: Japanese small plates on Müürivahe, in the Old Town. The salmon is lovely, and every other taste that came to the table was just as good. Go with 5 people, and order everything and try.
blurbs.kalve-kadriorg: Specialty coffee on the Kadriorg corner of Faehlmanni, roasted by Kalve. A few small tables out on the pavement, which is where you want to be when the sun is out.
blurbs.kartul: Fully vegan and built entirely around the potato, right by the tram stop in Telliskivi. Stuffed baked potatoes, homemade dumplings and sauces that pull it all together. Big portions, small prices. Read the first page of the menu before you order.
blurbs.karu-talu-sokolaad: A family-size cookie in the Old Town. They only prepare 300 if they are open. If you see the place open, grab usual cookie, and share with the people. One is enough for everybody.
blurbs.klorofull: A hidden gem on the second floor of the ARS art factory. Everything is made fresh and plant-based from local shops, and the menu changes weekly or more often than that. Go for lunch.
blurbs.koho: Restaurant, bakery and bar on the Telliskivi corner: floor to ceiling glass, plants everywhere and tables out on the pavement. Mediterranean cooking with a light Asian touch, and bread and their own hummus with every meal. Lunch is what I come for.
blurbs.koht: A small beer bar hidden on Lai 8 with more than 800 kinds of beer from all over the world. Start light, work up through the IPAs, finish on something dark. Ask the bartender. They know a lot and will help you choose.
blurbs.kokomo: Another definition for hyggelig. Super cozy vibes. Their baristas, coffees are so good, also try the sandwiches from menu (with kimchi or pesto) and also focaccia sandwich. They are improving. For me it is the best speciality coffee place in town, but nobody knows it yet. They will thrive.
blurbs.kotkot: Really nice chicken at Noblessner, and the chicken burger is the one to order. Get their card, and use the app for a discount before you pay.
blurbs.kringel: A vegan place with very good kringels. There is nothing to fault here. Hugely popular, and deservedly so.
blurbs.la-boulangerie: Even if I don’t like interior for some unknown reason, their pastries are delicious. Specially pistachio filled pastry you see in the photo. They are doing good stuff, so give a try.
blurbs.laboratooriumi-23: Foosball, sandwiches, drinks and a sauna, all in one place. Very diverse, very different from anything else you'll see in town. Finding it without Google Maps is a challenge.
blurbs.lendav-maaler: Used to be Georgian, now Mexican. It may not make sense at the beginning, but with each bite it starts to. The chicken taco needs extra work; the mushroom was the best.
blurbs.lokaal-tilk: A cozy vegan café blending Estonian, Asian and European flavours. Warming ramen, crispy portobello and homemade desserts. A great spot for a slow dinner with a twist.
blurbs.magussoolane: A bakery in Kadriorg where the sweet and the savoury are equally good. I usually run past this place, and the smell is what made me stop.
blurbs.maison-francois: A must-go bakery in the Old Town, best in the morning when everything is freshest. Known for high-quality croissants and desserts. Prices are reasonable for the quality, but this the place is closed, I would recommend François Boulangerie. But they are open only saturdays, so be ready for a long queue.
blurbs.mikkeller-old-town: Mikkeller is one of the biggest names in craft beer, and this one pairs it with real food. The kitchen is run by Viljandi Burger, which makes it a very good combination.
blurbs.mix-resto: A fine dining experience in the Old Town at lunch prices. Go for the three-course lunch menu. It is 20 euro. Menu is changing seasonly.
blurbs.morii-tea-house: New in Telliskivi and already second place for tea at the Helsinki tea and coffee festival. Come for the hojicha and genmacha.
blurbs.nullijook: An alcohol free bottle shop with a serious list. Amazing kombucha, Proxy drinks and de-alcoholised wines, so nobody at the table has to settle for water.
blurbs.paper-mill-coffee: Built in 1912 as the fire station for a massive Tallinn paper mill. Today it's a top 30 speciality coffee shop in Europe. Pastries and coffee are really cool. And you can see roasting process at the spot.
blurbs.paper-mill-coffee-volta: The second Paper Mill, out in the Volta quarter. A glass corner unit and a counter full of pastry they bake on the spot. The monkey bread is the reason to come. Pulling apart in pieces and eating like a croissant. Good coffee, delicious doughnuts and seasonal blueberry pastries are worth the trip.
blurbs.pilsneri-baar: Three different ways of pouring Pilsner Urquell, which is the whole reason to come. Proper Czech beer, and a nice garden to drink it in.
blurbs.pirosmani: Georgian food, big on flavour and generous in size. Portions are large and prices very reasonable, perfect for sharing with friends, and the food looks as photogenic as it tastes.
blurbs.porgandipomm: A properly hidden bakery in the Manufaktuuri quarter, and the baking is worth the finding. Been once, going back. I am coming back for those buns.
blurbs.pudel: A good place to bring a group and settle in for the evening. Really nice Guinness, and it is right there in Telliskivi. They were very nice to give tallinntastebuds discount, to be honest, without discount or anything the spot is nice. They used to be where Põhja Konn is, but their current spot is beautiful.
blurbs.pulla-bakery: Handmade sourdough buns baked by a mother and daughter in the heart of the Old Town. The place feels like a living room, and you might catch a fresh batch coming out of the oven.
blurbs.pohja-konn: Põhjala's own bar in Telliskivi, pouring their beers next to plenty of other craft. Take the balcony if it is free. I have to confess it is one of my favourite bar in Tallinn.
blurbs.puhaste-taproom: A Tartu craft brewery with a taproom on a busy Rotermann street. Their double IPAs are the reason to come, and the Silver collection is worth a look too.
blurbs.q-pizza-jaam: Pizza and sandwiches, and they bake the bread themselves. Go for the sandwich: it is finished in the wood fired pizza oven while you wait, and that is the whole reason to come.
blurbs.radio-restoran: Sharing is caring is the motto here, and it's the right way to eat. Just go and share whatever you see on the menu. You'll thank me, and so will your friends. Radio crispy chicken with cabbage salad was so good, also padrón peppers with seasalt.
blurbs.ramen-taro: My go-to meal has always been soup, and ramen taro has been the neighbourhood spot. Service and price are excellent. The taste is solid. Proper place for solo trip. Pro tip: Each weekday from 12:00 to 15:00 one ramen from menu is on discount.
blurbs.saffron: An Indian kitchen on Gonsiori. Soup, butter naan, garlic naan, special saffron naan, dessert, chicken saagwala. Everything was eaten to the last piece. I checked the other tables and everybody had finished their food completely. That is a sign.
blurbs.shaurma-kebab-linnamae: A Turkish kebab counter out in Linnamäe. From signature dishes to new items, we tried it all. Worth every penny.
blurbs.telliskivi-saslokk: Turkish cooking on the Telliskivi corner, and they bake their own bread. The lahmajun is the one to order. The place is found by Shaurma Kebab.
blurbs.the-brick-coffee: A coffee roastery with genuinely good food and a great feel to the room. One of the better places in town to take a date. I spent most of my time there, for one reason. It always feel warm.
blurbs.tuletorn: Tuletorn means lighthouse. The brewers from Põhjala decided they wanna make something better and they nailed it. If you want to try some decent craft beers. DDH, double IPA, smoothie beers, everything all at once.
blurbs.uba-ja-humal: Cheapest beer in the centre. Over twenty taps and a fridge full of more, and you can order a kebab from next door to eat in the bar.
blurbs.vaat-brewery: A craft brewery and taproom well out of the centre, and properly hidden at the moment. Reachable by bus or by bike, and worth the trip.
blurbs.vabrik: The cheapest wine in town, house pours and a proper list beside them, and it is a bottle shop too, so you can leave with one. In summer the tables go out on the pavement and that is where the whole point of the place is.
blurbs.vana-villem: A cozy local pub with old-school vibes, big portions and cheap beer. Open late and every day. Lots of snacks, cheap alcohol. Probably you will have long hours here.
blurbs.varkizana: A Greek tavern in Lasnamäe, and everything we tried was really good. Moussaka, tzatziki, souvlaki and dolma, and the moussaka is the one to come back for. The yoghurt dessert at the end was delicious too. Pro tip: call ahead and book your meal in advance.
blurbs.vegan-restoran-v: A vegan restaurant inside an old building in the Old Town, in the same spot for years. It is not fine dining and it is not cheap eats either: just good vegan food at reasonable prices, on plates that look the part. The room is very cozy. It is full of tourists, and if you are one looking for somewhere to eat in the Old Town, it is a good pick.
blurbs.veino: A small wine bar in the Old Town, run by people who are properly serious about wine. They know every bottle on the shelf and can talk you through any of them, and the shelves are full of interesting ones. Candles, a checkerboard floor, painted walls. Tell them what you like and let them pick.
blurbs.vesta: Vesta has arrived with small project, and now the restaurant is fully booked every day. All the menu is meant for sharing. The menu is changing from time to time. So each visit is different than previous. They got Michelin award for their service. Believe me service is the best part of the restaurant. Without an amazing team it wouldn't be possible.
blurbs.varav-coffee-toast: A little white house with a red roof at the end of a car park, right under the Old Town bastion, with the greenery on the sunny side. Kokomo beans through the La Marzocco, toasts, and a few tables out on the deck. The room is small, so laptops stay shut between 10 and 14; either side of that it is a good place to work, and a better one to just sit alone with a coffee.
blurbs.xinhai-1911: Chinese cooking by Balti jaam, and the hand-pulled biang biang noodles are the reason to come. One noodle, metres long, in chili oil and spring onion, with a broth on the side. Menu is long, but I am going there only for those noodles, after you finish noodles and the broth and finish the soup too. Watch the video, you would understand what I mean.
